summary: Round 3, test pass. All four round-2 fixes re-measured and all four KILL their mutation: the 4097-byte fixture kills the untrimmed put (measured admitting.length=8192 vs admitted=4097), the wiring case kills both the hardcoded-ceiling revert and the no-cache revert, the re-put case kills deleting the bytesHeld decrement, and the exact-N case kills the eviction > to >=. Four surviving mutations remain, all minor, none of them a regression from the round-2 fixes; the strongest is that SegmentProxy's use of segmentKey as the cache key is unconstrained.

findings.summary: Nothing constrains SegmentProxy to key the cache BY SEGMENT. Every case in the file puts exactly one key through one cache, so a proxy that consulted and filled the cache under any other key -- a constant, a prefix, a truncated key -- serves segment A's bytes to a consumer asking for segment B, and the whole suite stays green.
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED SURVIVING: SegmentProxy.java:218 'cache.get(segmentKey)' -> 'cache.get("mutant-constant-key")' together with SegmentProxy.java:294 'cache.put(segmentKey, ...)' -> 'cache.put("mutant-constant-key", ...)'. :ingest:test (229 tests), :http:test, :plugin:test and :client:test are all BUILD SUCCESSFUL. In production SubscriptionHub.publishSegment passes a distinct segmentKey per flush, so under any key-derivation regression the second publish of a DIFFERENT segment hits the first segment's entry and every consumer on that node is handed the wrong segment's bytes, silently and for as long as the entry lives -- strictly worse than the extra GET this row exists to remove. NOT a regression from the round-2 fixes: the gap has been there since round 1 and neither round raised it. Single-edit variants ARE killed (mutating only the get key, or making SegmentCache.get ignore its argument, is caught by GET counts and by aSegmentPutIsHandedBackBYTEForBYTE), which is why this is minor rather than major. One case closes it: two different segments through one proxy+cache, each publish asserted to receive its OWN bytes and the GET count asserted to be 2.

findings.summary: The HIT path's dead-consumer drop is untested. writeChunked duplicates the miss path's catch-and-remove, and the miss path is pinned in SegmentProxyTest while this copy has no case at all -- no test in SegmentProxyCacheTest uses a throwing sink on a hit.
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED SURVIVING: empty the body of the 'catch (IOException | RuntimeException slowOrDeadConsumer)' block at SegmentProxy.java:315-317 so live.remove(i) never runs -- :ingest:test green. A consumer that throws on chunk 1 of a CACHED segment then keeps being written to for all remaining chunks (each throw caught and swallowed), and streamTo returns live.size() counting a consumer that received nothing. On the miss path the same defect fails an existing test; on the hit path -- the path this commit adds, and the one production takes for every late subscriber -- it is invisible.

findings.summary: The wiring assertion restates the multiplier instead of constraining it: it asserts SegmentCache.DEFAULT_SEGMENTS_HELD * configuredSegmentBytes, so the constant appears on both sides and cannot be wrong.
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED SURVIVING: SegmentCache.java:50 'DEFAULT_SEGMENTS_HELD = 4' -> '= 1' leaves :ingest:test green. The assertion tracks the mutation (16 MiB on both sides), and the isNotEqualTo(DEFAULT_CAPACITY_BYTES) guard still holds because DEFAULT_CAPACITY_BYTES also moves, to 8 MiB. The deployed ceiling silently becomes ONE segment: a late subscriber to any publish but the most recent misses and issues a fresh GET, which is exactly the case M5.40b exists for, and bytesHeld() still reads plausibly. The javadoc says four is chosen and not derived, so pinning the literal 4 is arguably over-specification -- but then the case should assert a PROPERTY the constant cannot satisfy alone (for instance, strictly greater than one configured segment), not the product of the constant with itself.

findings.summary: The growth clamp Math.min(want, cache.capacityBytes()) is still unobservable, and forSegmentsOf's 4x ceiling does NOT make it reachable -- answering round 2's open question in the negative.
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED SURVIVING: '(int) Math.min(want, cache.capacityBytes())' -> '(int) want' leaves :ingest:test green. The clamp fires in exactly one case, aSegmentEXACTLYTheSizeOfTheCeilingIsCACHED (capacity 4097, want 8192), and the end-of-read trim at :294 copies the accumulator down to admitted=4097 either way, so the STORED array is identical with and without the clamp and every assertion in the file is satisfied. The clamp bounds the TRANSIENT peak only, and nothing in the suite measures a transient peak on a cached proxy -- criterion 6's cases build capacity-0 proxies, where no accumulation happens at all. Under forSegmentsOf the ceiling is 4x a segment, so the ladder for a normal segment never reaches the ceiling and the clamp is dead code there too; the only way it bites is a ceiling set below 2x a segment. Not worth a test through the present seam; recording it so the next reader does not re-derive it. Related and NOT a finding: 'admitted + read > admitting.length' -> '>=' at :254 also survives, but it is an equivalent mutant -- one extra doubling, byte-identical output.

findings.summary: Two dangling javadoc blocks -- javac warns 'documentation comment is not attached to any declaration' at both. The block at :210 reads 'A segment too big for the ceiling is served, and served again, and the ceiling is never breached', which describes aSegmentTOOBIGForTheCeilingIsStillSERVEDAndNeverRESIDENT at :250, but sits immediately above theINGESTERAPodActuallyRunsHasTheCacheON's own javadoc.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader opening the wiring case sees a one-line summary describing a different test, and the too-big case at :250 has no summary at all -- forty lines of separation between a description and the behaviour it describes is the stale-contract shape this task has blocked on twice already (M5.40a's @param segmentFanOut, SegmentProxy's own class javadoc). At :27 the same defect drops the NON-REPEATING fixture rationale: javadoc attaches only the LAST block before SEGMENT, so the measured explanation of why i*31+7 was vacuous is not in the generated docs. No claim in either block is false -- see the note field.

notes: MEASUREMENTS, all in a throwaway worktree at HEAD+staged patch, whole :ingest:test (229 tests) per mutation, build log checked for 'error:' and exit code checked so a non-compiling mutant cannot read as a survivor. Baseline green; restored tree re-verified green after the last mutation. KILLED: (1) trim removed, 'cache.put(segmentKey, admitting)' -- 2 failures, aHITIsHandedOverACHUNKAtATimeAndNotInONEWrite got 8 slices of 1024 instead of 5, and aFanOutOfSIXTYFOUR...'s late subscriber got 4095 trailing zeros. (2) DefaultIngest reverted to 'new SegmentCache(SegmentCache.DEFAULT_CAPACITY_BYTES)' -- theINGESTERAPodActuallyRunsHasTheCacheON fails. (2b) DefaultIngest reverted to 'new SegmentProxy(store)' -- same case fails. (3) 'bytesHeld -= replaced.length' deleted -- REPUTTINGAKeyReplacesItsBytesRatherThanAddingThem fails (300, not 100). (4) eviction '>' -> '>=' -- aCeilingOfEXACTLYNSegmentsHoldsNOfThem fails (bytesHeld 200, not 300). JAVADOC ARITHMETIC, checked: the 4097 paragraph is TRUE and measured -- at 4096 the ladder is 0->1024->2048->4096 with admitted == admitting.length, and at 4097 admitting.length ends at 8192 with admitted 4097, so the trim is taken in its real direction. The mod-256 claim is TRUE: 31 x 1024 = 31744 = 124 x 256, so b[i+1024] == b[i] for b[i] = (byte)(i*31+7) and every 1024-chunk of that fixture is byte-identical. 'four writes... five writes, not one' is TRUE (4 x 1024 + 1). The wiring comment is TRUE: IngestConfig.DEFAULT_MAX_SEGMENT_BYTES is 8 MiB, so DEFAULT_CAPACITY_BYTES is 32 MiB and 4 x 16 MiB = 64 MiB is a different number, which is what the isNotEqualTo guard pins. One phrase to read carefully rather than a false claim: aSegmentEXACTLYTheSizeOfTheCeilingIsCACHED's javadoc cites 'THREE > TO >= FLIPS SURVIVING'; it now kills two of them (SegmentCache.put's refusal, and SegmentProxy's 'admitted + read > cache.capacityBytes()'), and the third, the growth step at :254, survives as an equivalent mutant. TIER: theINGESTERAPodActuallyRunsHasTheCacheON takes Clock.systemUTC() into a T0 case, but it asserts no time and matches the established idiom in six other ingest test files, with the flush interval pinned to NEVER -- not a finding.
